title: The Youth Who Learned to Shudder
next_title: The Wolf and the Seven Little Kids
source: Grimm, Household Tales, tr. Margaret Hunt (1884), tale 4
lesson: Being brave doesn't mean feeling nothing.
lines: This boy wasn't afraid of anything, and that was his problem. I want to learn how to shudder, he told his father.
So the sexton dressed up as a ghost in the bell tower at midnight. The boy simply shoved the ghost down the stairs.
His father sent him away. Then he heard of a haunted castle: survive three nights, and win the princess.
Night one: black cats with fiery eyes. He chased them off, then slept on a bed that rolled round the castle.
Night two: ghosts playing skittles. He asked if he could join in.
Night three: a terrible old giant. The boy trapped his beard in an anvil, and won the treasure.
He married the princess, but still couldn't shudder. So she tipped a bucket of cold water and wriggling fish over him in bed. Now I know what shuddering is!
Being brave doesn't mean feeling nothing. Next time: the wolf and the seven little kids. Follow so you don't miss it!
